prompt:
I need the front end for Convene IEP. An in-house scheduling tool built by a large urban school district's special education department to set up legally required IEP meetings and coordinate the availability of parents, teachers, specialists and administrators within compliance deadlines.

Who's using it: Keisha Branford, a special education coordinator for 11 elementary schools in the district's North Region. She schedules around 30 IEP meetings a month, knows the federal and state timelines thoroughly, and uses the tool daily alongside the district's student information system.

What they're doing right now: Keisha is setting up the week after Thanksgiving break. A school psychologist, Dr. Lin, just went on unexpected medical leave through Dec 12, which affects six meetings that required her. Keisha has to decide which meetings can move to the substitute psychologist, which have to be rescheduled, and when, without missing any annual-review or 60-day initial-evaluation deadlines. Two families can only meet after 4 p.m., one needs a Somali interpreter, and the speech therapist covering three of the schools works only Tuesdays and Thursdays.

What's in the system at this point: Region roster: 11 schools, 214 students with active IEPs. 27 meetings in the Nov 30–Dec 18 window, each with: student (e.g., 'Amir H., grade 3, Whitfield ES'), meeting type (annual review, initial eligibility, reevaluation, amendment), compliance deadline (e.g., annual due Dec 4; initial 60-day due Dec 10), required participants by role (case manager, gen-ed teacher, LEA rep, school psychologist, SLP, OT, parent, interpreter), confirmation status per participant, room. Dr. Mei Lin: 6 affected meetings, leave Nov 20–Dec 12. Substitute psychologist Dr. Paul Ostrowski: available Mon/Wed/Fri at 4 of the 11 schools. SLP Rhonda Kim: Tue/Thu only. Interpreter pool: 2 Somali interpreters booked through district language services with 48-hour lead time. Parent availability notes from contact logs (e.g., 'Ms. Farah: after 4:15 p.m. only, prefers phone'). District closure days: Nov 26–28, Dec 21–Jan 1. Prior written notice must go to parents at least 10 days before each meeting.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
